title: North Bayou F80: A Budget Gas-Spring Monitor Arm — Check the Weight Limit
summary: The North Bayou (NB) F80 is one of the best-known budget gas-spring monitor arms: VESA 75/100, tilt, swivel and rotation, desk clamp or grommet mount. Its weight and screen-size limits matter more than anything else — here's what listings say.
description:
## Who is it for?

- Anyone whose monitor stand is tilt-only.
- Programmers who want portrait mode.
- Small desks that need the space under the screen.

## Why consider it?

- Gas-spring height adjustment, tilt, swivel and 360° rotation.
- VESA 75 × 75 / 100 × 100.
- Clamp or grommet mounting, internal cable routing.

sections.title: What is the North Bayou F80?
sections.content: North Bayou (often branded NB) is a Chinese maker of affordable monitor mounts, and the F80 is its best-known single gas-spring arm. It's sold by retailers worldwide, but specs vary between listings — and in some markets similar-looking arms from other brands are sold alongside or under the same listing. Make sure the product is the genuine NB F80.

sections.title: Check the weight and size limits first
sections.content: A gas-spring arm only works properly within its weight range: too heavy and the monitor sags, too light and it springs up. An Australian retailer lists the F80 at 17–27 inches and 2–6.5 kg, while other listings quote larger screens (up to 30 or 32 inches) and up to 9 kg. Weigh your monitor without its stand and compare it with the exact listing you're buying from. Most 24–27-inch monitors weigh 3–6 kg without a stand.

sections.title: Adjustment and ergonomics
sections.content: The arm offers about 250 mm of height travel, +35° to −50° tilt, 180° swivel and 360° rotation, so you can switch to portrait for coding or reading. Raising the screen to eye level helps neck posture, and freeing the space under the monitor gives you more desk room. It's especially useful if your monitor's stand is tilt-only, like the ASUS VG249QE5A or Xiaomi G24i.

sections.title: Installation
sections.content: The F80 clamps to the desk edge or mounts through a grommet hole. Check that your desk edge is solid and not too thick, and that there's no crossbar under the edge. You'll need to tune the gas-spring tension to your monitor's weight after mounting. Thin glass or particleboard desks may not hold the clamp well.

sections.title: Who should buy it — and who shouldn't
sections.content: Buy it if your monitor is within the listed weight range and you want height, swivel and portrait adjustment cheaply. Skip it for heavy or large ultrawide monitors, thin or fragile desks, or if you want a premium arm with a longer warranty (Ergotron, Amazon Basics' Ergotron-made arm).

sections.title: Sources for this review
sections.content: Zero Technology has not used this arm in person. This is a research roundup based on international retailer listings and the product manual, checked November 2026. Because listings disagree on screen size and load capacity, we quote the more conservative figures. North Bayou has no official website, so product images come from international retailer listings (The Wires Zone, AHW Store).

buying_advice: Great value — check your monitor's weight

faq.question: What monitor sizes does the F80 support?
faq.answer: An Australian retailer lists 17–27 inches; other listings go up to 30–32 inches. Weight matters more than size — check the load range.

faq.question: How much weight can it hold?
faq.answer: Listings range from 2–6.5 kg to 2–9 kg. Use the figure on the listing you buy from and weigh your monitor without its stand.

faq.question: Can I rotate my monitor to portrait?
Does my monitor need VESA holes?
faq.answer: Yes, 75 × 75 or 100 × 100 mm. Monitors without VESA need an adapter.

faq.question: Is installation difficult?
faq.answer: Usually 15–30 minutes: mount the clamp, attach the monitor, then adjust the spring tension.
